cur:catacombs-maius-virgin-child-orans.summary: In an arcosolium lunette a veiled woman with large eyes raises her hands in prayer, a child placed before her breast, between two chi-rho monograms. The painting has long been celebrated as one of the earliest images of the Virgin Mary with the Christ Child in prayer, a forerunner of the later 'Virgin of the Sign'.
facts: The chi-rho monograms – the first letters of Christ's name in Greek – flank the figure on both sides.
Commons classifies the image among 4th-century paintings of the Madonna and Child and among images of the 'Theotokos of the Sign' type.
cur:catacombs-maius-virgin-child-orans.notes: Many scholars think the woman may be the deceased with her child rather than the Virgin and Christ; the identification remains uncertain.

cur:objects3-breamore-rood.summary: Over the doorway in the porch of the Anglo-Saxon church at Breamore, a large stone rood shows Christ on the cross between the Virgin Mary and St John, beneath the hand of God reaching down from a cloud. The figures were cut back flush with the wall, probably at the Reformation, so that what survives is chiefly their outline and traces of medieval painting around them; even so the composition of the Cross between the two mourners is still plain.
facts: St Mary's, Breamore, is an almost complete Anglo-Saxon church; an Old English inscription of the reign of Æthelred the Unready survives on the arch to its south porticus.
The roundel of the Lamb of God set below the rood is a later, 12th-century addition.
cur:objects3-breamore-rood.notes: Badly mutilated; the date is approximate and usually given as around 1000. The Reformation as the occasion of the defacement is the usual explanation, not a documented fact.
